To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a joint optimization of transmitter, channel, and receiver can lead to a significant performance gain over the system with receiver-only optimization or no transmitter, channel, or receiver optimizations.

the joint optimization of transmitter waveform and linear receiver waveform for strictly band-limit linear modulations in cyclostationary Gaussian noise can lead to a significant improvement over the receiver-only optimized systems and the systems without optimizations.

the optimum transmitter and linear receiver waveforms, for strictly band-limted linear modulations in AWGN with a cyclostationary autocorrelation function and a period that is the inverse of the transmission rate, are derived and the numerical results show that the joint optimization of transmitter/receiver leads to a significant improvement over the systems that have no optimizations or only receiver optimizations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of optimizing the performance of a digital communication system operating in a cyclostationary environment, where the cyclostationary nature of the noise is known.
the problem of designing a joint optimal transmitter and receiver for linear modulations in the presence of cyclostationary additive noise.
the problem of joint transmitter and receiver optimization for strictly band-limits linear modulations in the presence of additive cyclostation-ary noise.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed joint optimization technique is the best one in the sense that it provides the lowest mean-squared error among all possible transmitter/receiver optimizations.
the joint optimization of transmitter waveform and receiver filter can lead to significant performance improvements in the presence of additive cyclostationnary noise.
joint transmitter-receiver optimization can lead to significant performance improvement over conventional systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the joint optimization technique is a powerful method that can be applied to any linear modulation in additive cyclo-stationary noise, and it leads to a significant improvement in the performance over the systems with only receiver optimization or no optimization at all.
the joint optimization of transmitter waveform, receiver filter and symbol timing is the best way to improve the performance of the receiver.

the optimum joint optimization of transmitter, receiver, and data sequence is achieved by the following steps: 1. Find the optimum data sequence as a WSS colored process by minimizing the mean-squared-error at the output of a linear receiver.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cyclostationary nature of the additive noise can be exploited for the design of a joint transmitter and receiver for linear modulations.
the joint design of transmitters and receivers is an important consideration for the performance optimization of communication systems.
, in the presence of cyclostationary additive noise, the transmitter and the receiver can be jointly optimized to improve the system performance.
